params.body:
Dates from feeds become ISO at intake, and one unreadable date no longer blanks a trend's strength.

**What went wrong**
- 1,073 signals, all from web feeds, carry a date like `Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:47:02 BST`. JavaScript can't read "BST" and gives `NaN`.
- `strengthOf` sums age weights over a trend's signals, so a single such date made the whole strength `NaN`, and it was stored as empty.
- Five trends never had a strength, three of them public. On the site and in the MCP they show `strength: null`, and there is no momentum on their page.

**Changes**
- **`core/dates.mjs`, `normalizeDate`:** turns a date into ISO. Time zone abbreviations with one meaning (BST, CEST, EST, JST, …) become their offset. Ambiguous ones (IST, CST) and non-dates give `null`, never a guess.
- **`makeSignal`** normalises `published_at` at intake. What can't be read falls back to the intake time, as before.
- **`strengthOf`:** a date it can't read counts as the intake date, then as one half-life. One bad date no longer spoils the sum.
- **`bin/fix-signal-dates.mjs`:** a one-time pass over the existing signals. It's dry by default, `--apply` rewrites, and the old value goes into `signal_date_undo`.

**After merge:** run `fix-signal-dates --apply`, then recompute strength for the five trends without one.

Checks: new `test/dates.test.mjs` (BST, CEST, GMT; IST and nonsense give null; `makeSignal` delivers a readable date). `insight-economy.test.mjs` gets a test that fails on the old formula ("strength NaN"). 955 tests, 0 failures.
params.title: Dates from feeds become ISO at intake, and one bad date no longer blanks a strength
